# Exercises - C Allpass Filters

## C Allpass Filters

Book page: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/filters/Allpass_Filters.html

#### `allpass-lossless-1` - difficulty 3; concepts: lossless, allpass, parseval

**Q.** Why must a lossless stable LTI filter satisfy |H(e^{jω})| = 1 for all ω?

- (a) Because the impulse response must be real
- (b) Parseval's theorem gives output energy = ∫|H|² |X|² dω; for this to equal input energy ∫|X|² dω for every X, we need |H|² = 1
- (c) Because the phase response must be linear
- (d) Because all poles are at the origin

Hint 1: Parseval relates time-domain and frequency-domain energy.

Hint 2: The equality must hold for every possible input.

**Answer: (b).** By Parseval, ||y||² = (1/2π) ∫ |H|² |X|² dω = ||x||² = (1/2π) ∫ |X|² dω for ALL X requires |H(e^{jω})|² = 1 (except possibly on a measure-zero set).

## C.1 Allpass Examples

Book page: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/filters/Allpass_Examples.html

#### `allpass-example-fir-1` - difficulty 2; concepts: allpass, fir, lossless

**Q.** Which FIR filters can be lossless (causal, allpass)?

- (a) Any FIR with all zeros inside the unit circle
- (b) Only filters consisting of a single nonzero tap: H(z) = e^{jφ} z^{-K} (a pure delay times a unit-modulus gain)
- (c) Any linear-phase FIR
- (d) Any symmetric impulse response

Hint 1: Need |H(e^{jω})| = 1 at every ω.

Hint 2: Multiple-tap FIR filters have non-constant amplitude responses.

**Answer: (b).** In the SISO case, only pure delays scaled by a unit-modulus constant are lossless FIR filters. All other FIR filters have a non-trivial amplitude response.

#### `allpass-iir-form-1` - difficulty 3; concepts: allpass, iir, polynomial-flip

**Q.** Every causal, finite-order, recursive (IIR) allpass filter can be written in the form \(H(z) = e^{j\phi} z^{-K} \tilde{A}(z)/A(z)\), where \(\tilde{A}(z)\) is:

- (a) The reversal (flip) of A(z), with coefficients conjugated when complex
- (b) The derivative of A(z)
- (c) The inverse polynomial 1/A(z)
- (d) The square A²(z)

Hint 1: Allpass: zeros are reflections of poles across the unit circle.

Hint 2: Polynomial flip is reversed-and-conjugated coefficients.

**Answer: (a).** Ã(z) = z^{-N} A*(1/z), i.e., reverse the coefficient order and conjugate complex coefficients. This reflects each pole of A across the unit circle to produce the zeros at 1/conj(p_i).

## C.2 Paraunitary Filters

Book page: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/filters/Paraunitary_FiltersC_3.html

#### `paraconj-def-1` - difficulty 4; concepts: paraconjugate, allpass, analytic-continuation

**Q.** The paraconjugate of H(z), written H̃(z), is defined as:

- (a) H(z̄) — conjugate the variable z
- (b) H̄(z^{-1}) — invert z (which is analytic) and conjugate the coefficients only
- (c) 1/H(z)
- (d) H(-z)

Hint 1: On the unit circle z^{-1} = z̄, so this reduces to ordinary conjugation there.

Hint 2: Analytic continuation requires an analytic transformation of z.

**Answer: (b).** H̃(z) = conj{H(1/z*)} = H̄(z^{-1}), where H̄ conjugates the coefficients only (not the powers of z). z̄ is not analytic; 1/z is.

## C.3 MIMO Allpass Filters

Book page: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/filters/Multi_Input_Multi_Output_MIMO_Allpass.html

#### `mimo-lossless-unitary-1` - difficulty 3; concepts: mimo, lossless, unitary, allpass

**Q.** A MIMO transfer function matrix H(z) (p outputs, q inputs) is lossless if and only if its frequency-response matrix H(e^{jω}) is what at every ω?

- (a) Diagonal
- (b) Symmetric
- (c) Unitary: H*(e^{jω}) H(e^{jω}) = I_q
- (d) Hermitian

Hint 1: Generalize |H|² = 1 to the matrix Hermitian-product = identity.

Hint 2: Energy preservation extends to vector signals.

**Answer: (c).** Losslessness ⇔ output energy = input energy for ALL inputs ⇔ H*(e^{jω}) H(e^{jω}) = I_q at every ω. Also requires p ≥ q (at least as many outputs as inputs).

## C.3.1 Paraunitary MIMO Filters

Book page: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/filters/Paraunitary_MIMO_Filters.html

#### `paraunitary-mimo-filters-1` - difficulty 1; concepts: paraunitary, mimo, allpass, paraconjugate

**Q.** The allpass property 1 = H(e^(jω))H(e^(−jω)) is generalized to the entire complex plane as H̃(z)H(z) = 1, where H̃ denotes the paraconjugate of H. In the MIMO (matrix) case, what does forming the paraconjugate additionally involve?

- (a) A matrix inverse
- (b) A matrix transpose
- (c) A determinant
- (d) Nothing extra -- it is identical to the scalar case

Hint 1: Think of how the Hermitian transpose generalizes complex conjugation from scalars to matrices.

Hint 2: The scalar operations stay the same; one purely matrix-level operation is added.

**Answer: (b).** In the MIMO case the paraconjugate is defined the same way as for scalar transfer functions but additionally includes a matrix transpose operation. This parallels how the ordinary conjugate transpose (Hermitian transpose) generalizes complex conjugation to matrices.

## C.3.1 MIMO Paraunitary Condition

Book page: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/filters/MIMO_Paraunitary_Condition.html

#### `paraunitary-cond-1` - difficulty 4; concepts: paraunitary, mimo, allpass

**Q.** A MIMO transfer-function matrix H(z) is paraunitary if it satisfies:

- (a) H(z) = H(z^{-1})
- (b) H̃(z) H(z) = I_q for all z (paraconjugate analytic continuation of the unitary unit-circle condition)
- (c) H(z) = H^T(z)
- (d) det H(z) = 0

Hint 1: Generalize H̃ H = 1 (SISO allpass) to the matrix case.

Hint 2: On |z|=1, paraconjugate reduces to Hermitian transpose.

**Answer: (b).** Paraunitary means the paraconjugate H̃(z) is the inverse of H(z) for all z. On the unit circle this reduces to the unitarity condition; off the unit circle it is the unique analytic continuation.

## C.3.1 Properties of Paraunitary Filter Banks

Book page: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/filters/Properties_Paraunitary_Filter_Banks.html

#### `paraunitary-fb-pr-1` - difficulty 4; concepts: paraunitary, filter-bank, perfect-reconstruction

**Q.** For a paraunitary FIR analysis filter bank, the perfect-reconstruction synthesis filter bank is:

- (a) An IIR filter bank
- (b) The paraconjugate filter bank — i.e., each synthesis filter is the (conjugate) time-reversal of its analysis filter, also FIR
- (c) The same analysis filter bank
- (d) A bank of allpass filters

Hint 1: FIR ⇒ paraconjugate is also FIR (just flip and conjugate coefficients).

Hint 2: Power-complementary channel filters Σ |H_k|² = 1 on the unit circle.

**Answer: (b).** If H̃ H = 1, then F = H̃ inverts the analysis filter bank, and since H̃ is the paraconjugate, F's filters are conjugate-flipped versions of the analysis filters (still FIR).
